subject: tu:game/movie/movieplayer
value: REFUTES THE STANDING RECOMMENDATION of claim.MP_movieplayer-flip-distance-chart.20260901.v1, measured 2026-09-01. The chart closes with: 'the highest-value single mechanism left in this TU is the r31-relative EH-island slot offset, which appears in fn_800D9C5C (+8), fn_800D96B0 (+8) and PlayVQMovie (three deltas) -- one construct plausibly unlocks three functions'. That framing is now measured false, in two separate ways, and no further lane should spend a run on it. (1) THERE IS NO SUCH CONSTRUCT for the two +8 carriers. fn_800D9C5C and fn_800D96B0 each need the island raised by 8 while the frame size stays EQUAL to the target's -- 72 in both functions, with the save set `stmw r28,56(r1)` also already equal on both sides. Per claim.law.EH_unexpected-island-offset-is-eh-block-start-plus-twelve.20260901.v1, derived from ~1370 compiles this run, the island offset can only be raised by giving the function a touched-but-dead ADDRESSABLE local, the shift is set by that local's ALIGNMENT and not its size, and an 8-aligned local -- the only thing that yields +8 -- always costs +16 frame bytes. The reachable (frame, island) lattice at the correct instruction count contains no (72, 28) cell, and the negative holds across eleven EH-region source forms, fifteen cleanup-action shapes, seventeen one-flag cflag deltas including `-RTTI on`, and ALL TWENTY compilers under build/compilers/GC. The prediction was then confirmed OUT OF SAMPLE on fn_800D96B0: the 8-aligned dead local moved its island r31+24 -> r31+36 and its frame 72 -> 88, real 8 -> 14, and was reverted. (2) THE THIRD FUNCTION IS NOT THE SAME MECHANISM AT ALL, so 'one construct unlocks three' was never available even in principle. PlayVQMovie is a MULTI-ISLAND function, and its islands do not share the single-island geometry the other two have: measured with fnasm --diff at frame parity (`stwu r1,-232(r1)` and `stmw r22,184(r1)` identical on both sides), its island at r31+76 ALREADY AGREES with the target, while a second island differs by +16 (target `addi r3,r31,28` at +0x5e4, ours `addi r3,r31,12` at +0x5f8) and additionally sits at a different stream offset, i.e. carries instruction drift the other two do not. Its inter-island spacing also disagrees -- 48 in the target against 64 in ours -- which is an island-COUNT/ordering question, not the below-block offset question the chart grouped it under. CONSEQUENCES FOR PLANNING. fn_800D9C5C is reclassified from the chart's 'one source word from a rule-closable exact' to BLOCKED: its blocking half is source-unreachable AND, being an immediate/operand difference, is barred from the postprocessor path by the Mandatory result policy, so its already-proven [3,0,1,2] epilogue permutation can never close it and must stay unauthored. fn_800D96B0 is capped on the same wall. PlayVQMovie's line in the chart should be REWRITTEN rather than deleted: it remains open, but as multi-island geometry with one island already correct, and it should be attacked through island count/ordering and its two large head clusters, never through the below-block lever that is now closed. Chart lines (1), (2), (5), (6), (7), (8), (9), (10) and (12) are untouched by this refutation and remain as measured.
